scope: In-process permission-cache invalidation versus database reads already in flight, including ownership changes. Not distributed authorization or full P2 acceptance.
implemented: Server middleware and channel single/bulk caches capture an invalidation revision before lookup. Cache publication and revision checks are serialized with invalidation; no cache mutex is held over database IO.

All/user/server/channel invalidation increments the relevant local resolver revision even when no cache row yet exists. A pre-invalidation database result cannot refill that cleared generation or be returned as a successful fresh grant.
Superseded lookups retry at most three times with context checks. Continuous mutation fails closed, rather than looping indefinitely or publishing stale permissions.
Bulk retries discard both cached and freshly fetched halves of a superseded snapshot; invalidated cached users are included in the fresh retry.
